In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects of social media annotation:
1) Tagging: We propose methods to improve the quality of user-generated tags, by leveraging social network information, visual and textual features, as well as temporal patterns of tag usage.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the research in this area is in its infancy, but the field is very promising and has the potential to make a major impact.
social image and video annotation is still a largely unexplored field, with many open problems and challenges.
the problem of automatically refining social tags is still open.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have proposed a number of novel methods and techniques for social tagging and localization, which have been shown to be effective and efficient in a range of experiments and applications.
we have proposed and developed a number of data-driven techniques for the automatic annotation of social media.

we have developed methods and algorithms for the automatic extraction of visual content and social metadata, for their integration in a single representation, and for the use of this representation to support the annotation and retrieval of visual content in social platforms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of social tags and annotations can be greatly improved through the integration of social and visual cues and the use of data-driven methods.
data-driven methods can be successfully applied to the problem of social tagging and can provide a useful complement to user-driven approaches.
the combination of data-driven approaches with the use of domain knowledge is a powerful approach for improving the quality of social image and video annotation.
